_comment: CRITERION OVERRIDES for the frozen BYOK border-design corpus (track byok_svg_borders_20260927).
A per-design `criterion` normally comes from the round file that WON the freeze (last-
accepted-wins), so the criterion a design is judged by is the one its frozen bytes were
generated for. That invariant is deliberately OVERRIDABLE, by an operator ruling: when a
criterion is re-cut WITHOUT regenerating the artwork (the bytes stay the winning round's),
the freeze takes the criterion from THIS file and records both texts on the fixture entry
(`criterion` = the override, `criterionGenerated` = the round file's text,
`criterionOverride` = the provenance). The override file is a freeze INPUT, so a fresh
freeze over the same rounds + this file is still byte-reproducible.
TWO overrides exist, both operator rulings made 2026-10-01 before any further gate run
(`phase4_operator_rulings_20261001.md` §1 D-C, `phase4_operator_rulings_r2r3_20261001.md`):
D-C — 04-dragon-scale's scale rows are judged aspect-independently because the product's
`border-image` edge scaling is ANISOTROPIC on a tall section (~0.146 px/unit horizontal vs
~0.923 vertical with `round` on 656x1920), so square scales become vertical slivers on the
left/right rails while the top/bottom rails keep the source's own proportions. The render
knob did NOT move; the criterion did.
R-3 — 01-gilded-frame's criterion demanded a GOLD tone, which the product's own default
decoration filter (`grayscale(100%)` at the shipped defaults, applied to every border kind
through the same `::before` slot) makes unsatisfiable by construction: measured on the
judged frame, gold-classified pixels 0.0000% on the TOP band while the frozen blob's gold
#c9a227/#d4af37 renders as the luma-161 grey the band measures. Under operator ruling R-2
(the judged instrument stays at PRINT defaults), the criterion is re-cut to the SHAPES the
pipeline actually paints — measured on the same frame: two concentric rules continuous on
every edge (TOP 96.9%/95.7%, BOTTOM 95.5%/96.9%, LEFT 98.9%, RIGHT 98.6-99.0% line
coverage; the only break runs are the corner junctions where the perpendicular rules meet,
which is the ring's own structure, not a dash pattern) and a diamond-shaped corner mark at
each of the four corners (ink inside the diamond box the frozen blob's own coordinates
predict: 113/94/104/91 px against 72 px in an identical control box on the same rails —

04-dragon-scale.criterion: Overlapping scale shapes are drawn in rows along the border, each scale visibly tucked under or over its neighbour; the individual scales are judged where the pipeline paints them at the source's own proportions — the top and bottom rails — and the left and right rails must carry the same overlapping-row texture even where the pipeline's anisotropic edge scaling narrows the individual scales.
04-dragon-scale.supersedes: Overlapping scale shapes are drawn in rows along the border, each scale visibly tucked under or over its neighbour, and the rows read as the same texture on the left/right as on the top/bottom.
04-dragon-scale.reason: Operator ruling D-C: the frozen 4c blob (800x800, filled paths) is deformed by anisotropic border-image edge scaling on the 656x1920 gallery section; the ruling re-cut the criterion aspect-independently and kept the render knobs unchanged, so the criterion now judges the source's proportions where the pipeline preserves them and only demands texture (not aspect) on the anisotropic rails.

01-gilded-frame.criterion: Two concentric rectangular rules run as continuous SOLID lines along every edge — each rule unbroken from corner mark to corner mark around the full rectangle, no dash pattern and no mid-edge break in either rule — and both rules are present on all four edges, with a diamond-shaped corner mark at each of the four corners. The rules are judged by SHAPE, continuity and doubling only: the product's default print filter renders the whole band in greyscale, so no hue is expected in the judged frame and an absence of colour is NOT a failure of this criterion.
01-gilded-frame.supersedes: Two concentric rectangular rules in a gold tone are both drawn as continuous SOLID lines closed around the full rectangle — no gaps or dashes anywhere on either rule — a diamond mark sits at each of the four corners, and no rule crosses the interior.
01-gilded-frame.reason: Operator ruling R-3 (paired with R-2, which keeps the judged instrument at the product's PRINT defaults): the frozen round-5b blob strokes `url(#goldGrad)` #c9a227/#d4af37, and a clean-Chromium reproduction of the shipped border-image pipeline paints that band gold (8.3% gold px), but the product's own default decoration filter — `grayscale(100%)` at the shipped defaults, applied to every border kind through the same ::before slot — removes the hue before any pixel exists. Measured on the judged native cell, the band is the greyscale of the authored gold (luma 161) and gold-classified pixels are 0.0000% on the TOP band; a colour-demanding criterion is therefore unsatisfiable by construction for ANY artwork, not just this one. The ruling re-cuts the judged TEXT to the shapes the pipeline does paint — two concentric rules continuous on every edge plus a corner mark at each corner, both measured on the judged frame — and keeps the frozen bytes (sha256 99605fc3…, round 5b) unchanged.
